passages.text: Symptoms of active tuberculosis (TB) disease depend on where the TB germs are growing in the body. Common symptoms of active TB disease include cough, pain in the chest, and coughing up blood or sputum (phlegm).

A bad cough that lasts 3 weeks or longer
Pain in the chest
Coughing up blood or sputum (phlegm) from deep inside the lungs
Weakness or fatigue
Weight loss
Loss of appetite
Chills
Fever
Sweating at night
People with inactive TB do not have symptoms of TB disease. However, without treatment, they can develop active TB disease and become sick.
